text: This frozen turkey is dropping into a pot of oil that's 350 degrees.
say: This frozen turkey is dropping into a pot of oil that's three hundred and fifty degrees.

But there's still ice packed inside it.
The second that ice melts, the water sinks into the hot oil.

text: Water boils at 212 degrees, so it turns to steam right away. And steam takes up about 1,700 times more space than water.
say: Water boils at two hundred and twelve degrees, so it turns to steam right away. And steam takes up about seventeen hundred times more space than water.

All that steam has to go somewhere, so it shoves the boiling oil up and over the top of the pot.
And when that oil hits the flame below, the whole thing turns into a fireball.
It's a big reason Thanksgiving has almost four times more cooking fires than a normal day.
Follow for more, because this is why you should never fry a frozen turkey.
